title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 18.

questions.question: Who did David smite and subdue, taking Gath and her towns from their control?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:1 states that David smote the Philistines and took Gath and her towns from them.

questions.question: What was the status of the Moabites after David smote them?
options: They became David's servants and brought gifts
They formed an alliance with David
questions.correctAnswer: They became David's servants and brought gifts
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:2 records that after David smote Moab, the Moabites became his servants and brought gifts.

questions.question: David smote Hadarezer king of Zobah as he went to establish his dominion by which river?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:3 specifies that Hadarezer was going to establish his dominion by the river Euphrates when David smote him.

questions.question: How many chariots did David take from Hadarezer king of Zobah?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:4 says David took a thousand chariots from Hadarezer.

questions.question: What did David do to most of the chariot horses he captured?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:4 states that David houghed all the chariot horses but reserved one hundred chariots.

questions.question: How many horsemen did David take from Hadarezer?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:4 records that David took seven thousand horsemen from Hadarezer.

questions.question: How many footmen did David capture from Hadarezer king of Zobah?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:4 notes that David took twenty thousand footmen from Hadarezer.

questions.question: How many Syrians did David kill when they came to help Hadarezer king of Zobah?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:5 states David slew twenty-two thousand Syrians when they came to assist Hadarezer.

questions.question: After defeating the Syrians of Damascus, what did David do in their land?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:6 reports that David put garrisons in Syria Damascus after defeating the Syrians.

questions.question: True or False: The Syrians became David's servants and brought gifts after he put garrisons in their land.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:6 confirms the Syrians became David's servants and brought gifts after he stationed garrisons.

questions.question: True or False: David reserved all the chariots he captured from Hadarezer without damaging any horses.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:4 explains that David houghed all the chariot horses except for those of one hundred chariots.

questions.question: True or False: David smote the Philistines and took Gath and her towns out of their hand.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:1 clearly states that David smote the Philistines and took Gath and her towns from them.

questions.question: True or False: David smote the Edomites and put garrisons in Edom according to 1 Chronicles 18:12.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:12 discusses Abishai slaying Edomites, but the garrisons in Edom and their servitude to David are found in verse 13, not 12.

questions.question: Which event happened first according to 1 Chronicles 18:1-6?
options: David put garrisons in Syria Damascus
David smote Hadarezer king of Zobah
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:1-6 presents the order: first David smote the Philistines (v.1), then Moab (v.2), then Hadarezer (v.3), then he took spoils (v.4), slew Syrians (v.5), and finally put garrisons in Syria Damascus (v.6).

questions.question: What did David do with the shields of gold taken from the servants of Hadarezer?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:7 states that David took the shields of gold from Hadarezer's servants and brought them to Jerusalem.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did David do with the shields of gold taken from the servants of Hadarezer?
options: He sold them to the Philistines
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:7 states that David took the shields of gold from Hadarezer's servants and brought them to Jerusalem, demonstrating his authority and honoring God with the spoils.

questions.question: From which cities did David bring much brass, used later by Solomon for the brasen sea and pillars?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 18:8, the brass David brought from the cities of Tibhath and Chun was used by Solomon to make important temple furnishings, showing the continuity of God's blessings.

questions.question: How did King Tou of Hamath respond after hearing about David's victory over Hadarezer?
options: He sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David
questions.correctAnswer: He sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:9-10 describes that Tou sent his son Hadoram to David to inquire about his welfare and congratulate him for defeating Hadarezer, reflecting respect and political diplomacy.

questions.question: What did David do with the gold, silver, and brass vessels he received from various nations?
options: He dedicated them to the LORD
He gave them to his soldiers
questions.correctAnswer: He dedicated them to the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:11 states that David dedicated the silver, gold, and brass vessels brought from the nations to the LORD, showing his faithfulness and gratitude to God.

questions.question: How many Edomites did Abishai kill in the valley of salt?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 18:12, Abishai, son of Zeruiah, slew eighteen thousand Edomites in the valley of salt, demonstrating David's continued military success.

questions.question: What was the result of David putting garrisons in Edom?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:13 explains that after placing garrisons in Edom, the Edomites became subject to David's rule, showing God's preservation of David's kingdom.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 18:13 promise will happen if the LORD preserves David whithersoever he goes, as seen in verses 6 and 13?
options: David’s servants will become servants to him
questions.correctAnswer: David’s servants will become servants to him
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 13 describe the LORD preserving David wherever he went, resulting in the Syrians and Edomites becoming his servants, revealing God's faithfulness in rewarding obedience.

questions.question: How does the dedication of spoils to the LORD in verse 11 teach about Christian generosity and humility?
options: It shows that leaders should keep all treasures
It demonstrates giving God the glory for victories and blessings
It encourages accumulating wealth for personal gain
It indicates that gifts should be hidden
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates giving God the glory for victories and blessings
questions.explanation: Verse 11 shows David dedicating spoils from many nations to the LORD, teaching us to humbly recognize God as the source of all blessings and to generously honor Him.

questions.question: True or False: David's military success was solely due to his own strength and wisdom.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:6 and 1 Chronicles 18:13 emphasize that the LORD preserved David wherever he went, indicating that God's protection and favor were crucial to David's victories.

questions.question: Who was appointed over the host during David’s reign according to verse 15?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:15 states that Joab, son of Zeruiah, was over the host, indicating his leadership role in David's military forces.

questions.question: What role did Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud have in David’s administration?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:15 identifies Jehoshaphat as the recorder, responsible for documenting the king’s deeds and events, showing the importance of record keeping.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 18:14, David was a just ruler who executed judgment and justice among all his people.
questions.explanation: Verse 14 states that David reigned over Israel and executed judgment and justice, teaching us the importance of justice and righteousness in leadership.

questions.question: Who were the priests serving during David's reign as mentioned in verse 16?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:16 lists Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar as the priests, indicating their spiritual leadership roles.

questions.question: How does the passage about David dedicating spoils (v11) linked with his military victories teach about faith and obedience?
options: Success comes from human effort alone
Faith and obedience result in God’s blessing and rightful praise
Spoils should be hidden to avoid envy
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and obedience result in God’s blessing and rightful praise
questions.explanation: Verses 3-5 show David’s military obedience, and verse 11 shows dedication of spoils to God, teaching that faithful obedience leads to God's blessing and honoring Him is essential.

questions.question: Who was over the Cherethites and Pelethites during David’s reign according to verse 17?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:17 states that Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites, showing his military leadership over elite troops.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 18.

questions.question: Who was appointed over the host (army) during David's reign according to 1 Chronicles 18?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:15 states that Joab, son of Zeruiah, was over the host, meaning he was commander of the army.

questions.question: What role did Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud have according to 1 Chronicles 18?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:15 clearly identifies Jehoshaphat as the recorder, responsible for keeping records.

questions.question: Which two priests served during David's reign as mentioned in 1 Chronicles 18?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:16 names Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar as the priests serving under David.

questions.question: What was the position of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada during David's reign?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 18:17, Benaiah was over the Cherethites and Pelethites, elite guards serving the king.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Thus the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went' in 1 Chronicles 18:13 indicate about David's military campaigns?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:13 emphasizes that the LORD preserved David, indicating that his victories were attributed to divine protection rather than mere human effort.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 18:14, what two qualities did David execute among all his people?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:14 states David executed judgment and justice, highlighting his role as a righteous and fair king.

questions.question: Which foreign king sent his son to congratulate David, bringing gifts after his victory over Hadarezer?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:9-10 describes how Tou king of Hamath sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David and bring gifts after David defeated Hadarezer.

questions.question: What did David do with the gold, silver, and brass vessels he brought from various nations as recorded in 1 Chronicles 18?
options: Used them to pay his army
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:11 explains that David dedicated the precious metals and vessels to the LORD, showing his devotion and acknowledging God's blessings.

questions.question: Which battle resulted in Abishai slaying eighteen thousand Edomites according to 1 Chronicles 18?
options: Battle in the valley of salt
questions.correctAnswer: Battle in the valley of salt
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:12 records that Abishai slew eighteen thousand Edomites in the valley of salt, a significant military victory.

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated in the phrase 'Thus the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went' appearing twice in 1 Chronicles 18:6 and 1 Chronicles 18:13?
questions.explanation: The repetition of 'Thus the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went' at both the beginning and near the end of the narrative sections creates an inclusio, framing David's successes with divine preservation (1 Chronicles 18:6, 18:13).

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'garrisons' in 1 Chronicles 18:6 and 13 most closely means what?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'garrisons' (mispôt) refers to military posts or detachments placed to secure a region, as seen in 1 Chronicles 18:6 and 18:13.

questions.question: Which earlier Old Testament passage foreshadows David's role as a just and righteous king similar to the description in 1 Chronicles 18:14?
questions.explanation: Psalm 72 is a royal psalm that describes the ideal king executing judgment and justice, foreshadowing David's reign as portrayed in 1 Chronicles 18:14.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of divine preservation and victorious leadership found in 1 Chronicles 18:13?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:31 states 'If God be for us, who can be against us?' which echoes the theme of divine preservation and victory as seen in 1 Chronicles 18:13.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 18:17, the sons of David held positions of authority close to the king.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:17 states that the sons of David were chief about the king, indicating their authoritative roles near him.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Chronicles 18:4 describes David sparing all the chariot horses he captured from Hadarezer.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:4 says David 'houghed all the chariot horses, but reserved of them an hundred chariots,' meaning he disabled most horses except for a hundred chariots.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine is demonstrated by David dedicating the silver and gold brought from conquered nations to the LORD?
options: The doctrine of stewardship over earthly treasures
The doctrine of God's sovereign provision and rightful ownership
The doctrine of justification by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's sovereign provision and rightful ownership
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:11 shows David dedicating spoils from various nations to the LORD, indicating that all wealth ultimately belongs to God, affirming His sovereign ownership over creation (see Psalm 24:1).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly revealed by the statement 'Thus the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went'?
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 13 both affirm that the LORD preserved David wherever he went, showcasing God's providential care and guidance over His anointed king (1 Chronicles 18:6,13).

questions.question: How does the conquest of the Philistines and taking of Gath (1 Chronicles 18:1) contribute to the biblical narrative of redemption?
options: It fulfills the promise of rest and land to Israel
It shows Israel's independence from God
It illustrates the sinfulness of war
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the promise of rest and land to Israel
questions.explanation: David's defeat of the Philistines and capturing of Gath represents the fulfillment of God's promise to give Israel rest from enemies and possession of the land (see Joshua 21:44; 1 Chronicles 18:1).

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining 1 Chronicles 18:3-4 and 18:5-6 regarding God's role in David's military victories?
options: God's role is limited to moral support
God actively grants victory and subdues enemies through David's leadership
Victory is due to David's military genius alone
questions.correctAnswer: God actively grants victory and subdues enemies through David's leadership
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 describe David’s victories over Hadarezer’s forces, while verses 5-6 emphasize that the LORD preserved David wherever he went, indicating divine empowerment and blessing in his military success.

questions.question: Which doctrine is best taught by David placing garrisons in conquered territories such as Edom and Damascus?
options: The doctrine of the Church's spiritual authority
The doctrine of God’s kingdom extending through political rule
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God’s kingdom extending through political rule
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 13 show David establishing control through garrisons, illustrating how God's kingdom is manifested not only spiritually but also through righteous governance and dominion over nations (1 Chronicles 18:6,13).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that biblical accounts of conquest promote violence and are morally problematic. What does 1 Chronicles 18:11 teach about the purpose of David's spoils from war?
options: They were kept for personal gain
They were dedicated to the LORD as an act of worship and acknowledgment of God's sovereignty
They were used to oppress conquered people
They were distributed to foreign allies
questions.correctAnswer: They were dedicated to the LORD as an act of worship and acknowledgment of God's sovereignty
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 18:11 states that David dedicated the silver and gold from conquered nations to the LORD, showing that the spoils were offered to God, not kept for personal enrichment, thus framing conquest within divine purpose and worship.

questions.question: What does the act of David 'houghed all the chariot horses, but reserved of them an hundred chariots' (1 Chronicles 18:4) symbolize in theological terms?
options: God's judgment on reliance on human strength rather than divine help
David's desire to increase his cavalry
A political alliance with the chariot owners
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment on reliance on human strength rather than divine help
questions.explanation: By disabling the chariot horses except for a hundred, David reduced reliance on military might and demonstrated that victory comes by God's power, reflecting trust in divine sovereignty over human strength (1 Chronicles 18:4).

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 18:10–11 illustrate the theme of covenant fellowship in God's redemptive plan?
options: By showing political alliances replacing God’s covenant
By showing neighboring kings sending gifts to David, who dedicates them to God, indicating inclusion in God's covenant blessings
By ignoring foreign nations’ role in Israel's history
By focusing only on Israel's internal affairs
questions.correctAnswer: By showing neighboring kings sending gifts to David, who dedicates them to God, indicating inclusion in God's covenant blessings
questions.explanation: Verse 10 describes the king of Hamath congratulating David with gifts, and verse 11 shows David dedicating these gifts to the LORD, symbolizing God's covenant extending influence beyond Israel’s borders.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by the statement 'Thus the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went' seen in both 1 Chronicles 18:6 and 18:13?
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase in verses 6 and 13 emphasizes God's active and faithful protection over David’s reign, underscoring His providence and covenant faithfulness (Ps 121:7-8).

questions.question: What does the role of Joab as 'over the host' (1 Chronicles 18:15) teach about leadership in God's kingdom?
options: Leadership is based solely on military strength
God appoints leaders to execute His justice and protect His people
Leadership is irrelevant in spiritual matters
questions.correctAnswer: God appoints leaders to execute His justice and protect His people
questions.explanation: Joab’s military leadership under David's reign shows that God ordains leaders to govern and defend His people, reflecting divine order and justice in governance (Romans 13:1-4).

questions.question: How do 1 Chronicles 18:7 and 18:8 collectively contribute to understanding the theme of sacred worship in the Davidic monarchy?
options: They show David’s disregard for temple worship
They highlight the gathering of spoils to create temple vessels, emphasizing worship centered on the LORD
They focus solely on military conquests
They promote idolatrous use of spoils
questions.correctAnswer: They highlight the gathering of spoils to create temple vessels, emphasizing worship centered on the LORD
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 describe David taking gold and brass from defeated kings to Jerusalem, used by Solomon to make temple items, illustrating the integration of conquest into worship and sanctification (1 Chronicles 18:7-8).

questions.question: What combined theological teaching emerges from 1 Chronicles 18:2 and 18:12 about God's sovereign rule over nations?
options: God allows nations to act independently without consequence
God subjugates nations under His appointed king, making them servants to Israel
God is indifferent to political affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God subjugates nations under His appointed king, making them servants to Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 2 explains the Moabites became servants to David, and verse 12 shows Abishai killing Edomites, who also became servants, reflecting God's sovereign authority over nations through David's rule (1 Chronicles 18:2,12).

questions.question: How does the mention of Benaiah over the Cherethites and Pelethites (1 Chronicles 18:17) contribute to understanding the role of royal guards in the Davidic kingdom?
options: They served as religious leaders only
They symbolized the king’s personal protection and divine election
questions.correctAnswer: They symbolized the king’s personal protection and divine election
questions.explanation: Benaiah’s oversight of the Cherethites and Pelethites, elite guards, signifies the royal protection around the king, reflecting God's chosen monarchy and the safeguarding of His anointed (1 Chronicles 18:17; 2 Samuel 8:18).

questions.question: What narrative arc is reflected by David's reign over all Israel and executing judgment and justice (1 Chronicles 18:14) in the context of biblical kingship?
options: The failure of human kings to rule righteously
The ideal of a king ruling under God’s law and justice, foreshadowing the Messiah’s perfect reign
The irrelevance of kingship in Israel’s history
The replacement of divine law with human decrees
questions.correctAnswer: The ideal of a king ruling under God’s law and justice, foreshadowing the Messiah’s perfect reign
questions.explanation: David’s just reign embodies the biblical ideal of righteous kingship, pointing forward to Christ, the righteous King who perfectly rules with justice (1 Chronicles 18:14; Isaiah 9:6-7).

questions.question: What theological insight arises from combining 1 Chronicles 18:9-10 and 18:11 about God's providence and kingdom expansion?
options: God’s kingdom is limited to Israel alone
God sovereignly uses international relations to expand His kingdom and bless His anointed king
Foreign nations always oppose God’s people
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly uses international relations to expand His kingdom and bless His anointed king
questions.explanation: The king of Hamath congratulates David and sends gifts (verses 9-10), which David dedicates to God (verse 11), showing God’s providential orchestration of kingdom growth and blessing beyond Israel.
